info.name: BOT Rejection
info.description:
BOT document-rejection coverage for MSIL_PARTNER / Delhi. Self-contained: it onboards its OWN
driver and vehicle rather than reusing 01-HappyPathOnboarding's entities, so a rejection cycle
can never leave the happy-path collection's asserted end state broken.

SHAPE
  Setup runs the full onboarding EXCEPT the final BOT approvals — that leaves each entity at
  verified=true, sitting in the BOT queue. The reject API requires exactly that state
  (unless driverInfo.verified / rcInfo.verified /= Just True -> 'not verified'), so the happy
  approve is replaced by the first rejection instead of being done and then undone.

  Then, once per MANDATORY document:
    BOT reject that document -> assert the entity falls out of verified
    -> re-supply it through the same onboarding API -> recompute -> BOT approve
    -> assert verified / enabled / approved restored.

EXCLUDED DOCUMENTS
  ProfilePhoto — the API refuses it outright ('Cannot reject Profile Photo').
  Permissions  — mandatory in config but absent from the status document list, so rejecting
                 it is a silent no-op (invalidateSpecificDocument falls through to pure ()).

Re-supply is document-specific because invalidateSpecificDocument differs per type: some
documents have their own record set INVALID (DL/Aadhaar/PAN/VRC) and must be re-registered,
some are image-only, LocalResidenceProof also clears the stored address, VehicleInspectionForm
invalidates every vehicle image at once, and the InspectionHub types set the operation hub
request to REJECTED — which needs a fresh request plus a new operator approval.

ORDER MATTERS: each entity's setup is immediately followed by its rejection block, and the FLEET
OWNER block runs BEFORE the fleet vehicle and fleet driver blocks. Setup deliberately omits the
happy BOT approval, which leaves the fleet verified but NOT enabled — and addVehicle/addDriver
reject an un-enabled fleet owner ('Fleet owner is not enabled'). The fleet owner's own
reject -> re-supply -> approve cycle is what enables it, so the fleet vehicle and fleet driver
flows reuse an enabled fleet.

Uses the same Local_MSIL_Delhi environment as 01.

// password login resolves the person but returns authToken="" with the message
// '2 Factor authentication is not enabled, it is mandatory for this deployment'.
// The MSIL admin credential is minted in step 02 instead, from the seeded
// registration_token — see the TOKENS note in the collection description.
console.log('is2faMandatory:', d.is2faMandatory, '| is2faEnabled:', d.is2faEnabled, '| merchantId:', d.merchantId, '| city:', d.city, '| message:', d.message);
// Exercises cross-merchant access: the Bangalore/NAMMA_YATRI-scoped admin token is
// re-scoped to MSIL_PARTNER/Delhi and a fresh LoginRes.authToken comes back.

// Fresh operator identity on EVERY execution of this step.
